brief.headline: Close the ₹16.09 L price gap and shorten payment by 15 days to free ₹5.31 L cash — Mars Plastics and three bigger alternates give us the muscle.

priceAsk.summary: Match Mars Plastics' price on bottles and caps — that closes the gap entirely.
priceAsk.target: ₹1.38/NOS for the 30 ml bottle (we pay ₹1.65), ₹0.81/NOS for the 28 mm cap (we pay ₹0.90), ₹2.20/NOS for the 60 ml bottle (we pay ₹2.25). Total saving: ₹16.09 L/year.
priceAsk.basis: Mars Plastics and Cincorp International Ltd. already give us these prices for identical items. The 28 mm cap market asks run ₹0.55–1.20/pc (typically ₹0.85–0.95), so ₹0.81 is fair — in fact, at higher volume the market could go as low as ₹0.65–0.80.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Move from 45 days to 30 days after receipt.
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Frees ₹5.31 L of our cash every 15 days; over a year that compounds to real working funds we can deploy elsewhere.

brief.financialLeverage: Premier Plastic publishes no financials, so we can't see their profit, debt or how tight cash is for them. Our ₹1.29 Cr annual spend is real money to a private converter, but without their numbers we lean on the market: Mars already delivers at these prices, and we've lined up Manjushree Technopack (₹2569.83 Cr revenue, health score B 65/100) and Mold-Tek Packaging (₹1010.97 Cr, health B 73/100) as credible second sources. That competition — not their balance sheet — is our leverage.

evidence.point: We pay ₹16.09 L a year more to Premier than the lowest price we already get from other suppliers for the same items.
On the 30 ml HDPE bottle, Premier charges ₹1.65/NOS while Mars Plastics supplies it at ₹1.38/NOS — a 19.6% gap costing us ₹11.74 L/year.
On the 28 mm PP cap, Premier is ₹0.90/NOS versus Mars at ₹0.81/NOS — an 11.1% gap worth ₹4.23 L/year.

The open-market asking price for a 28 mm induction-wad PP cap sits at ₹0.55–1.20/pc (typically ₹0.85–0.95), and the analysis says 'MARKET-FAIR; modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume / looser spec' — so ₹0.81 is well within fair territory.
Cutting payment terms from 45 days to 30 days frees ₹10.63 L of our working capital; even a 15-day reduction releases ₹5.31 L.
HDPE resin import prices stand at 87.61 ₹/kg, giving us a transparent raw-material benchmark if they cite cost pressure.

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter (₹2569.83 Cr revenue, health B 65/100) — pharma bottles, caps, preforms — a top second-source candidate already qualified for our packaging.

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader (₹1010.97 Cr revenue, health B 73/100) making pails, containers and pharma packaging — strong and profitable, a robust alternate for bottles and closures.

alternates.name: Hitech Corporation Ltd
alternates.why: Listed moulded and blow-moulded packaging house (₹701.17 Cr revenue, health C 51/100) with broad capability across bottles and caps.

risks: Premier's finances aren't public, so we can't gauge how fragile they are — push hard on price but keep the tone collaborative so we don't break a supplier we might still need.
Mars Plastics already beats them on the two biggest SKUs; if Premier won't move, be ready to shift more volume to Mars and bring in Manjushree or Mold-Tek as a second line.
The ₹16.09 L gap is an estimate based on our purchase history — verify the exact annual quantities and SKU mix before you lock a number in the room.
The market backups (Reliance, Srichakra, IVL Dhunseri, Dalmia, Ganesha, Chemco) are leads to qualify — don't treat any as approved or priced until we've done due diligence and an RFQ.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We value the partnership, but Mars Plastics is already giving us ₹1.38 on the 30 ml bottle and ₹0.81 on the cap — we need you at that price to keep the business here, and we'd like to move to 30-day terms so both sides free up cash.
